title: Diet contrasts in drought abundance responses changed sign across five bird studies in a 2024 release
abstract: We compared drought abundance responses of insect-eating and seed-eating birds within five studies in a 2024 public data release. We used 119 rows and 99 study-metric-species units. Equal-species mean contrasts were negative in three studies and positive in two. The equal-study mean was -0.286 source effect-size units. Removing the North Dakota study changed the mean to +0.012. Both North American studies had negative contrasts; three Australian studies had mixed signs. Medians kept all five signs. Matching location and released drought magnitude changed one small Australian contrast to negative. The proportion of species with negative responses gave a different summary. Source publication years do not supply independent drought-period tests. Shared droughts, few seed-eating species, different metrics, detection and publication bias limit inference. These fixed-release descriptions do not establish a causal diet effect or its absence. The package gives code, aggregate evidence, a figure, source hashes and external retrieval instructions. It tests no air pollution effect.

display.caption: Insect-minus-seed contrasts in five studies. The left panel compares mean and median source responses. The right panel compares fractions of species with negative responses. Points are fixed-data descriptions, not confidence limits.

citations.reason: Source and study-identifier audit informs a new within-study diet contrast. Records overlap; code is new.
